title.narrative: Advancing Gender Transformative Agrifood Systems & Nutrition Governance in Kenya

description.narrative: Despite women comprising 65% of the agricultural workforce in Kiambu County, they're limited to lower level, less profitable activities and excluded from key decision-making processes due to entrenched patriarchal norms. This reduces efficiency and impacts food security and nutrition. The high incidence of gender-based violence (GBV) further hampers women's ability to contribute effectively to the agri-food sector and assume leadership roles.The project aims to empower women by increasing their participation in governance and decision-making within agricultural value chains, advocating for equitable land ownership, and implementing measures to mitigate GBV.It seeks to create a more inclusive, resilient agrifood system, fostering gender equality and improving nutrition and food security.

Direct target group of the project comprises 2,627 participants from the agricultural and food system and its (political and economic) management organizations, of whom at least 60% are women and 20% are young people. 190 leaders of producer groups, 1.100 smallholder farmers, 340 aggregator groups, 300 women-led processing groups, 60 leaders of trade associations, 270 small business owners, 105 government representatives, 12 women leaders in agri-food systems, 70 representatives of civil society organizations, 60 community leaders, 15 private sector actors, 20 national-level political actors in parliament and the senate, 20 representatives of district parliaments, 5 women in political and high-level leadership positions, 5 regulatory institutions and 50 representatives of the media.The indirect target group comprises the members of the participants' households; with an average of five people per household, this means 13,135 people.

Overall objective: Food security and living conditions in Kiambu have improved thanks to a gender-equitable agricultural and food system.Project objective: 2,627 actors in the agri-food system in Kiambu County and at national level use their knowledge of gender transformative approaches and accountability to actively participate in the agri-food system and food policy.
